newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican building industry faces tough times - CSS.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican building industry faces tough times - CSS.

text.p: South Africa's building industry faces a bleak future after the first nine months of 1996 saw only a 2.1 percent rise in the value of new building plans passed, the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said.
"The prospects for the industry do not look so good," a CSS statistician told Reuters.

The CSS said in a separate statement the future performance of the industry would be sluggish as only 13.93 billion rand of new plans had been passed in the period -- a net rise of just 291.6 million rand.
The biggest geographical contributors to the stunted growth were the provinces of KwaZulu-Natal, which saw a drop of 21.7 percent, and the Orange Free State, which saw a fall of 8.8 percent.
The CSS said the value of plans for residential buildings had fallen by 2.4 percent to 6.58 billion rand as the number of plans for townhouses and flats dropped sharply.
The causes for the decline were difficult to pin down, the statistician said, but it was probably another symptom of the general slowdown of the South African economy.
"It is the general slowdown in the economy. We have seen the same thing in other industries like manufacturing and mining," she said.
There are some tentative signs that the value of plans for small dwellings may rise strongly soon and give a boost next year.
"There are signs, but really we are only hoping," the statistician said.
